subject.title: [Feature]: SSRF 内网访问确认机制

question: Should OpenClaw add a browser private-network SSRF confirmation or allow/block policy, and what core policy shape is approved?
rationale: The request changes browser egress controls and public config/CLI surface; current source has no confirm or temporary-grant contract that automation can safely extend without maintainer security intent.

options.title: Approve a staged core policy
options.body: Start with narrow allow/block policy plus non-overridable metadata/link-local behavior, then consider interactive confirmation after the security contract is tested.

options.title: Approve interactive confirmation now
options.body: Define the full user-approval UX, timeout, rate-limit, audit, redirect, and DNS-rebinding semantics before implementation begins.

options.title: Keep current strict model
options.body: Leave strict default, hostname exceptions, and broad trusted-environment opt-in as the supported browser SSRF policy for now.

recommendation.title: Approve a staged core policy
recommendation.body: Start with narrow allow/block policy plus non-overridable metadata/link-local behavior, then consider interactive confirmation after the security contract is tested.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest sampled history across the browser SSRF config, guard, docs, and security-boundary surfaces involved in this decision.
